text:
mike: Seeing a p99 latency bump on TP fused-attn jobs in us-west-2 dedicated pool since the 2026-03-09 deploy. Baseline ~48ms -> now ~63ms for short sequences (seq=256). Profiling points to more frequent fallback from flash-attn packed kernel to the shuffle+allgather path.

mike: quick profile dump (sampled):
```
kernel: flash_attn_qkv_packed_v1  count=121  avg=34.2us
kernel: flash_attn_qkv_shuffle_allgather_v3  count=98  avg=112.7us
allreduce: nvcc_allreduce    count=98  avg=30.1us  -> often overlapping poorly with compute
kvcache: hit_rate=0.87  miss_rate=0.13 (spike vs baseline 0.04)
```

mike: note the shuffle kernel count correlates with sequences that have small token prefix variance (lots of short prompts mixed with long ones). Suspect batching heuristic + kernel selector is mis-predicting contiguity of QKV layout and falling back.

elyse: do we have the kernel selection trace for one of the slow RPCs? can you dump the selector decision flags?

mike: pasted one trace from a failing request:
```
selector: requested_kernel=flash_attn_qkv_packed_v1
fallback_reason=noncontig_qkv_layout
heuristic: batch_contig_ratio=0.42  threshold=0.6
action: route_to=flash_attn_qkv_shuffle_allgather_v3
comm_plan: TP_allgather then local_compute
```

jordan: ah okay. so if batch_contig_ratio < threshold we pick the shuffle path which does per-tensor allgather. For TP with N=4 that multiplies allreduce traffic. If overlap isn't scheduled right we pay full latency.

sam: when the runtime falls back we also disable KV prefetching for that request because the layout is no longer contiguous. that explains the kvcache miss bump.

elyse: do we know why the batching heuristic saw low contig ratio? Is it due to our greedy batch packing mixing user types?

mike: yes — seen in traces: a few user requests with many short live-chat interactions get batched with background long-generation jobs by the default packer. Pack size limit and max_latency cause heterogeneous batches. The selector assumes qkv stride stability within a batch which is false here.

jordan: quick mitigation: we can adjust packer to prefer homogenous qkv_layout groups: add a small batching key of (qkv_layout_type) before pack. low risk and cheap.

sam: longer term, we need to improve kernel selector confidence scoring. Option ideas: (1) use a fast pre-check that simulates contiguity on representative members of the batch, (2) keep flash_attn fallback path but schedule an aggressive comm/compute overlap: kick off allreduce on Q and K while compute streams warm up.

mike: I ran an experiment on staging: forcing homogenous packing (group by contig flag) reduced shuffle kernel calls 92% and p99 dropped back to baseline. no model changes.

mike: logs from staging run:
```
2026-03-12T17:02:13Z packer: group_by_qkv_layout=on, batches=512, avg_batch_homogeneity=0.96
2026-03-12T17:02:13Z runtime: flash_attn_qkv_shuffle_allgather_v3  count=8  avg=118.4us
2026-03-12T17:02:13Z runtime: flash_attn_qkv_packed_v1 count=504 avg=33.1us
2026-03-12T17:02:13Z p99_latency_ms=49.1
```

elyse: awesome. Can you open a quick PR to make group_by_qkv_layout=true default for Dedicated TP pools and add a feature flag? We can A/B it for a week. Also add telemetry metric from selector: "selector_fallback_reason" counts.

mike: filing PR now — attaching patch id 9f2c3ab. Also adding selector_fallback_reason telemetry.

infra-bot: deploy queued for staging: rollout/packer-group-by-qkv-layout  (owner: mike)

jordan: small note: for hybrid TP+PP topologies, grouping might reduce multiplexing benefits. So opt-in for PP pipelines or add a conservative threshold.

sam: +1 on selector telemetry. Also adding a micro-optimization: when fallback happens, we can pre-schedule the allgather on a high-prio CUDA stream and then kick compute on the default stream to improve overlap. I'll prototype.

mike: plan for tomorrow: 1) land packer PR behind ff, 2) telemetry + dashboards for fallback reasons, 3) sam to prototype comm/compute overlap tweak, 4) run 48h canary on dedicated pool.

elyse: thanks team. assign to eng-runtime sprint board under card PERF-2983. Sam, Jordan, Mike listed as assignees.

jordan: if we see this again after packer change, we should trace NVLink counters: allreduce retries and PCIe fallback. That will narrow hardware-level cause.

sam: noted. I'll add perf counters to the selector debug dump.

mike: ok closing here for now — will update once PR merged and staging canary results are in. :thumbsup:
